headline: Nvidia saves the Nasdaq, not the market: Waller's half-point talk sets the tone for the close
tone: Risk off underneath a tech bounce. The day turned on the Fed, not on Nvidia: once Governor Waller floated a 50bp December hike, the dollar, metals, miners and value stocks all priced a tighter Fed, and only AI hardware held its gains.
body: Nvidia's beat bought chip stocks a relief day, but it did not broaden. The Dow and Europe's cyclicals carried the weight of hike bets, and the S&P 500 finished its fourth straight losing day still under its 200-day average, the level traders now treat as the line between a pullback and a correction.

The driver was Waller telling CNBC the Fed should consider a 50bp hike in December, citing core services inflation above 3% in about 70% of items and three straight 0.3% monthly core CPI prints. The October minutes at 20:00 were read the same way, so the hawkish pricing went into the close unchallenged.

Metals took the hardest hit because they lose most from a stronger dollar and higher real rates; the selling spread to gold and copper miners, including the Lundin names. Bitcoin's slide below $63,000 fits the same picture of leverage being pulled out of anything without a yield.

Crude closed lower on the stock build and weak refining margins, but late claims from Iran that three tankers hit mines east of Hormuz (unverified, after the close) are the risk for tomorrow's open. A US Navy official put single-transit insurance at $64 million against $54,000 a year ago, which is a cost on every cargo even if no barrels are lost.

views.text: Priced in for tomorrow: a Fed that hikes in December, possibly by 50bp. Walmart (14:00 Zurich) is the read on whether the US consumer is holding up under that; a soft jobless claims or Philly Fed print at 14:30 is the only near-term thing that could talk hike bets down and broaden the rally beyond chips.

Oil is trading the US supply glut over Gulf risk for now. If the Hormuz mine reports are confirmed, the premium comes back fast in crude, freight and TTF; if they fade like the Bandar Abbas blast scare, the soft-demand story keeps the lid on.

findings.summary: Fed Governor Waller said the Fed should consider a 50bp December hike, pointing to broad core services inflation; gold and silver fell as hike bets and the dollar rose.
